result.verdict: ADEQUATE — Passes 100% full-backing reserve requirement under MiCA Article 36(1).

tail_convention: For reserve coverage ratio, the LOW tail (coverage < 1.0) is adverse. This baseline test verifies that the current ratio (1.02) lies safely above the minimum threshold of 1.0.
weakest_point: Assumes fair market values of reserve assets reflect real-time liquidatable value without considering execution slippage or liquidation delays.

result.verdict: REQUIREMENT_COMPUTED — Minimum required own funds set to 2,000,000.00 EUR under MiCA Article 35(1) parameterization.

tail_convention: For own-funds adequacy, the LOW tail (actual own funds < required own funds) is adverse. This test computes the minimum threshold parameter to define the adverse boundary.
weakest_point: Uses a single static percentage parameter (2%) for reserve assets without applying the tiered/scaled bracket structure if additional tiering rules apply.

result.verdict: INADEQUATE — Fails 100% full-backing reserve requirement under MiCA Article 36(1) under adverse stressed market conditions.

tail_convention: LOW tail is adverse. The stress test specifically evaluates the downward movement (adverse tail) of reserve asset valuations to verify if coverage drops below 1.0.
weakest_point: Haircut percentages are static inputs and do not model dynamic correlation shocks or liquidity freezing across asset classes.

result.verdict: ADEQUATE — Full redemption satisfied at par without fee under MiCA Article 39 / Article 49; post-redemption coverage ratio remains above 100% (102.35%).

tail_convention: For redemption execution, the LOW tail of payout ratio (actual payout / guaranteed par value < 1.0) is adverse. This test verifies exact 1:1 redemption (ratio = 1.0).
weakest_point: Assumes immediate liquidity availability in reserve assets to fulfill large cash redemptions without forcing fire sales.
